node.title: Re: detecting an undefined variable
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Using an non-existant variable is a fatal compilation error under [doc://strict] (which one should always use). This smells of [https://perl.plover.com/varvarname.html|using a variable as a variable name, which is generally considered a bad practice]... why would you want to do this, what do you need this for?

Normally, the solution to this kind of thing would be to use a hash instead, where the [doc://defined] and [doc://exists] checks apply (with the differences explained in their documentation).

Enough rope to shoot yourself in the foot: For package variables, one can use if ( defined $::{'VARNAME'} ) ... (Update: although this checks for any symbol with that name, including arrays, hashes, subs, etc. - one could use peek_our from [mod://PadWalker] instead, similar to the following example), and for lexical variables use PadWalker qw/peek_my/; if ( defined peek_my(0)->{'$VARNAME'} ) .... But don't do this.
